newsitem.title: VATICAN: Tired Pope calls for prayers before operation.
newsitem.headline: Tired Pope calls for prayers before operation.

text.p: Pope John Paul asked the world's Roman Catholics to pray for him on Sunday as he prepared to enter hospital for surgery to remove his appendix.
"Tonight, I will enter hospital to undergo an operation," the Pope, 76, told tens of thousands of people in St Peter's Square.
"In asking you to accompany me with your prayer, I send cordial greetings to those in hospitals and clincs, knowing I can count on their spiritual solidarity.
"May the caring Virgin Mary watch over all of us," he added in remarks to the crowd at the end of a beatification ceremony where he put 16 more Catholics on the road to sainthood.

The Pope, who has had major abdominal surgery three times since 1981, was due to enter Rome's Gemelli hospital on Sunday evening after a Vatican announcement last month that he was suffering from recurrent inflammation of his appendix.
He is likely to undergo the operation on Tuesday.
Some medical experts and Italian media have expressed scepticism over the official version of what is ailing the Polish-born leader of the world's 960 million Catholics.

The Pope looked tired at times during Sunday's ceremony, which lasted almost three hours. He coughed several times while reading his homily from a throne below the balcony where he made his first appearance as Pope after his election in 1978.
The green-robed Pontiff's left hand trembled markedly as it has for at least the past three years.
The Vatican has not denied recent media reports in Italy and France, and the opinion of some doctors, that the trembling may signal Parkinson's Disease or some other neurological disorder.
The Pope, who marks the 18th anniversary of his pontificate on October 16, praised the newly beatified, the penultimate step leading to sainthood in the church.

They included 13 fellow Poles massacred by Russian soldiers for their loyalty to Rome in 1874, a Spanish and a Polish nun and Irishman Edmund Ignatius Rice, the founder of the Christian Brothers teaching order now spread throughout the world.
Many thousands in the crowd were fellow Poles waving the red and white national flag, adding to the poignancy of the event.
The Vatican said last month that periodic inflammation of the appendix was the cause of three bouts of "intestinal fever" which have ailed the Pontiff since Christmas.
Earlier this week, the Vatican denied an Italian news agency report that the Pope may be suffering from a new tumour. He had a colon tumour removed in 1992.
Professor Giorgio Ribotta, one of the doctors who signed a September 14 statement saying the Pope had an appendix problem, called reports of a tumour "medical fiction -- an Italian sport".
Ribotta said the operation could last about an hour although it could take longer in the Pope's case because parts of his intestine had already been removed in previous operations.
Some was removed in 1981 following an assassination attempt and more was taken out with the colon tumour in 1992.
The Pontiff and close aides will stay in a special, heavily-guarded suite with its own chapel and a view of the dome of St Peter's Basilica on the 10th floor of the Gemelli.
His stay there will be the sixth of his papacy since 1978.

The Pope underwent major abdominal surgery twice in 1981 after he was shot and almost killed by Turkish gunman Mehmet Ali Agca and again in 1992 to remove the colon tumour, which doctors said was starting to turn malignant.
He also had hip replacement surgery in 1994 after breaking his right leg in a bathroom fall and dislocated his right shoulder, which needed re-setting, in 1994.
